purpose: Dense research layer for understanding the Farm as an attention ecology rather than a list of lolcows.
epistemic_rule: Public attention, archival counts and documented events are empirical. Farmer, Dog, Cow, Milk, Mud, Sektur and Farm are project analytical vocabulary. No person is presumed to be a victim, perpetrator or participant merely because an archive discusses them.
core_model: subject -> exposure -> observer network -> documentation -> reaction -> secondary production -> amplification -> archive -> monetization/status -> renewed exposure

historical_definition.origin_note: The term is commonly traced to the cash-cow metaphor: a person repeatedly producing material that an audience can 'milk' for entertainment. Know Your Meme records an early Urban Dictionary definition from April 15 2007 and an Encyclopedia Dramatica article from December 2007.
historical_definition.important_shift: The modern Farm is broader than the original insult. It can include archival communities, documentary creators, fans, critics, journalists, platforms, algorithms, monetization and political audiences.

ecosystem_roles.cow: A person or public persona that has become a recurring object of collective attention.
ecosystem_roles.farmer: An actor who cultivates attention around a subject by documenting, commenting, provoking, analyzing, streaming, editing, archiving or otherwise producing material.
ecosystem_roles.dog: An actor who repeatedly follows, reacts to, attacks, defends, challenges or amplifies a subject. The term is project vocabulary, not a claim about a person's character.
ecosystem_roles.audience: People who consume, share, comment on or financially support the material.
ecosystem_roles.archive: The accumulated memory layer: threads, videos, screenshots, articles, wikis, court records, social posts and mirrors.
ecosystem_roles.platform: The technical and economic infrastructure distributing attention.
ecosystem_roles.milk: Observable attention output: views, comments, watch time, posts, donations, subscriptions, advertising, fundraising and status.
ecosystem_roles.mud: Accumulated negative or contested traces: allegations, conflicts, humiliations, legal filings, corrections, sanctions and reputational events.
ecosystem_roles.repair: Correction, apology, restitution, moderation, reconciliation, disengagement, deletion, retirement or other processes that reduce or transform the cycle.

system_measurements.interpretation: Page count measures archival production, not importance, guilt, harm, truth or moral worth. It is a measurement of attention infrastructure.

farm_dynamics.alpha_omega: A figure can be alpha-like when attention begins around them and omega-like when the archive becomes larger than the original person. The distinction is symbolic, not a ranking of human worth.
farm_dynamics.farmer_following: Farmers follow high-yield subjects because subjects provide recurring narrative material. This can be deliberate content production or emergent behavior by audiences.
farm_dynamics.dog_following: Dogs follow because reaction itself produces content. A dog can become a farmer when their reactions become an independent content stream.
farm_dynamics.cow_reaction: The subject can become an active producer of the Farm by responding, fighting back, livestreaming, correcting, escalating or attempting to monetize attention.
farm_dynamics.feedback: subject reaction -> audience reaction -> creator reaction -> subject reaction is a positive feedback loop that can persist even when every participant claims to dislike the process.
farm_dynamics.platform_effect: Recommendation systems, notifications, search, reposting and archives reduce the cost of finding previous material and therefore make historical material reusable as fuel.
farm_dynamics.death_effect: Death can end primary participation while increasing archival value: old material becomes fixed, commemorated, disputed or remixed. Death therefore changes the state of a Farm rather than necessarily deleting it.
farm_dynamics.repair_effect: Apology, correction, disengagement, moderation, legal resolution, reconciliation or loss of audience can interrupt the loop. A complete model must measure these exits rather than assume endless escalation.
